title: Recall gives
subtitle: the page back.
summary: Every page change goes through one ledger: change-only writes, exact restore, and a newer host edit always wins.
lead: Every change Fizlet makes to the page goes through one ledger. It records the original and what the engine wrote. `destroy()` puts back everything the engine still owns, newest first, and the DOM matches the snapshot taken before. That is Recall: the reason a game can knock a page's headings around and leave nothing behind.

items.title: `ledger.text(node, value)`
items.body: A text node's value: the 0s and 1s a shot leaves in a word. `fizlet/board-page` writes into the page's own Text nodes this way, with no wrappers or clones.

items.title: `ledger.style(el, prop, value)` and `unstyle`
items.body: One inline style property: a transform, a custom property. A style attribute comes back byte for byte. `unstyle` puts one property back now and forgets it.

items.title: `ledger.add(node)`
items.body: A node the engine put on the page (a canvas, an overlay, debris). Recall removes it.

items: **Change-only.** Writing the value that is already there makes no mutation. A browser test writes the same value twice and counts zero.
**Host wins.** If the host page changed something after the engine did, the ledger stops writing it and never restores over it. A write returns `false` when the host got there first.

**Exact.** After `destroy()` the DOM matches a snapshot taken before the engine started, attribute for attribute and style text byte for byte. One `AbortSignal` also removes every listener and observer.

body.text: `engine.ledger.restore()` is Recall without destroying the engine; the **Recall** key on the [home page demo](/) runs exactly that. Bricks that own an element (the touch pad, the perf overlay, the match overlay) add it through the ledger, so `engine.destroy()` takes them too.

items.q: Why not just reload the page?
items.a: Because the page is someone else's. A reload loses their state, their scroll and their form fields. Recall undoes only what the engine did, and leaves everything else as the visitor left it.

items.q: What if my code writes the DOM directly?
items.a: Then Recall can't give it back. Write through `engine.ledger` (or a brick that does) in `render`, and the page comes back exactly.

seo.title: Recall: how Fizlet gives the page back
seo.description: Fizlet's ledger records every DOM change: change-only writes, an exact restore on destroy(), and a newer edit by the host page always wins.
